Indian Holidays 2026 / भारतीय अवकाश कैलेंडर 2026

भारत में हिन्दू, मुस्लिम, ईसाई, सिख और अन्य समुदायों के त्योहारों के साथ राष्ट्रीय दिवस भी मनाए जाते हैं। नीचे 2026 की प्रमुख छुट्टियाँ और खास दिन महीने के हिसाब से दिए गए हैं।

This list covers the main festival days, national days and observances for 2026, across Hindu, Christian, Sikh and Muslim traditions. Which of them is a public holiday depends on your state and employer, so treat it as a planning guide and check your official holiday notice.

Things to keep in mind / ध्यान दें

  • Only a few days, such as Republic Day (26 January), Independence Day (15 August) and Gandhi Jayanti (2 October), are observed as holidays across the whole country.
  • Most other public holidays are decided state by state, so the same festival can be a holiday in one state and a working day in another.
  • Islamic festivals follow local moon sighting, so the date can shift by a day. Dates marked "expected" in the table are the likely ones.
  • Central government holidays are notified every year by the Department of Personnel and Training. Banks follow the RBI holiday list for each state.

स्थानीय राज्य की छुट्टियाँ वहाँ की धार्मिक और सांस्कृतिक परंपराओं पर निर्भर करती हैं। अपने राज्य और संस्थान की आधिकारिक सूची ज़रूर देखें।

For the Hindu festival dates with their tithi, see the Hindu Calendar. For South Indian festivals, see Telugu Festivals.

Indian Holidays FAQs

How many national holidays are there in India?

Three days are observed across the whole country: Republic Day on 26 January, Independence Day on 15 August and Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October. Other holidays are declared by the central government list or by each state.

Why do Eid and Muharram dates change?

Islamic months start with the sighting of the new moon, so the date depends on when the moon is seen locally and can differ by a day.

Is every festival in this list a holiday?

No. The list includes festivals, jayantis and observances. Whether an office, school or bank is closed depends on your state and organisation.

Dates are for Delhi (IST) and may differ by a day in other cities or traditions. Confirm important festivals with your family pandit.
